Exercise 4: CI Strategy Decisions

28 points
Choose the best approach for each competitive intelligence challenge.
Scenario 1 7 points

You want to build a living CI system but don't know where to start. Your team tracks 6 competitors manually. What's the recommended first step?

Build monitoring for all 6 competitors simultaneously
Pick your #1 competitor and build the full pipeline end-to-end first
Wait until you have engineering resources to build a custom solution
Focus on improving your existing quarterly battlecard process
Scenario 2 7 points

Your agent-powered CI system detects 50+ competitor signals per week. Sales is overwhelmed and ignoring the alerts. What's the fix?

Send fewer alerts by filtering to only major announcements
Create a weekly digest email with all 50 signals
Route specific insights to specific people — deal-relevant intel to AEs, product news to SEs
Train sales to check the CI dashboard more regularly
Scenario 3 7 points

An AE asks: "What should I know about Competitor X for my call tomorrow?" How should a living CI system respond vs traditional approach?

Point them to the Q3 battlecard in the sales enablement portal
Generate a deal-specific brief based on this prospect's industry and recent competitor moves
Schedule a call with the competitive PMM to discuss
Send them links to competitor's recent press releases
Scenario 4 7 points

Your AI finds that Competitor X mentions "data security" 3x more often in calls than last quarter. What's the PMM's role?

Add "data security" as a keyword filter for future monitoring
Interpret WHY — is it a new product, a competitive response, or market trend? Then brief sales accordingly
Create new battlecard content about your data security features
Share the statistic directly with the sales team via Slack
